descriptionChirho: To apply oil ritually to a person (king, priest, prophet) or sacred object (tabernacle, altar) in order to consecrate or set apart for divine service.
To receive sacral anointing, expressed through the Nifal stem or Qal passive participle, describing the state or event of being set apart by oil application.
To apply a substance (paint, plaster, cosmetic oil) to a surface or one's body for non-sacral, physical purposes such as painting walls or personal grooming.
